mission_01: Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) are the most widely used features in speech recognition, capturing the spectral envelope of speech in a compact representation that mimics human auditory perception. The MFCC extraction pipeline begins with pre-emphasis, a high-pass filter that boosts high-frequency components to balance the spectrum since speech energy decreases with frequency. The signal is then divided into short overlapping frames (typically 25ms with 10ms hop) to capture quasi-stationary segments, and each frame is multiplied by a Hamming window to reduce spectral leakage. The Fast Fourier Transform converts each frame to the frequency domain, and the power spectrum is computed. The mel filter bank applies triangular filters spaced according to the mel scale, which approximates the non-linear frequency resolution of the human ear (linear below 1000 Hz, logarithmic above). Taking the logarithm of the filter bank energies compresses the dynamic range, and the Discrete Cosine Transform decorrelates the coefficients, producing the final MFCCs. In this mission, you will implement the complete MFCC extraction pipeline from raw audio signal to cepstral coefficients.
